questions.question: Summarise the mechanisms of the term: define mechanical advantage, state the gear direction and ratio rules with a worked example, and describe what a cam and a crank each do.
questions.expected_answer: Mechanical advantage is load divided by effort; above 1 multiplies force, below 1 multiplies speed, and distance is always the price. Meshing gears counter-rotate; an idler restores the driver's direction without changing the ratio. A small driver turning a large driven gear gives a slower, stronger output and vice versa; velocity ratio is driver teeth over driven teeth and the force ratio is its inverse, so 10 teeth driving 30 gives velocity ratio 1:3 and mechanical advantage 3. A cam on a rotating shaft lifts and drops a follower once per turn, converting rotary to reciprocating motion (eccentric wheel smooth, snail cam slow rise and sudden drop). A crank is an arm on an axle acting as a second-class lever with mechanical advantage of arm length over axle radius; with a connecting rod and slider it converts between rotary and reciprocating motion.

questions.question: Summarise the structures of the term: the four forces, the forces in a king post truss, why pylons are triangulated lattices, the five spanning types, and the three failure modes with their cures.
questions.expected_answer: Tension pulls, compression pushes, shear slices across, torsion twists. In a king post truss the rafters and struts are in compression and the tie beam and king post in tension. Pylons are open lattices because loads run through legs and bracing; cross-bracing triangulates every panel so it cannot rack and stops legs buckling; the wide base gives stability. Spanning: beams bend (deep is stiff, I-beam saves material); suspension bridges hang from draped anchored cables; cable-stayed bridges use straight stays to a tower; arches work in compression and need abutments; cantilevers are fixed at one end and bend at the root. Failures: fracture is lack of strength, cured by more or better material and bigger joints; bending and buckling are lack of stiffness, cured by depth, tubes, triangulation and bracing; toppling is lack of stability, cured by a wide base, low centre of gravity and anchoring.

questions.question: Summarise the design skills of the term: the IDMEC design documents, the line, scale and dimensioning conventions, and the purpose of the three kinds of drawing.
questions.expected_answer: IDMEC: investigate, design, make, evaluate, communicate. The brief states the problem (user, need, kind of product, setting) without the solution; specifications are testable musts and constraints are limits of size, materials, time, cost and tools; several annotated idea sketches are compared in a table; making follows a cutting list and sequence safely; evaluation tests each specification and gives strengths, weaknesses with causes and improvements; communication presents the whole story. Lines: dark outlines, feint construction, dashed hidden detail, chain centre lines. Scale is drawing to real, 1:2 half, 2:1 double, real sizes always written. Dimensions in mm with no unit, outside the view with projection lines, arrowheads and figure above, once each, overall sizes given, holes from centre lines. The working drawing is a flat, fully dimensioned single view for the maker; the isometric shows the object in 3D along axes at vertical and 30 degrees to explain how it fits together; the artist's impression uses colour, shading and texture to show appearance for the client.
